title: 1992 AHSME Problem 18
statement: The increasing sequence of positive integers \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(a_3,\) \(\ldots\) has the property that, for every \(n\ge1,\) \[ a_{n+2}=a_n+a_{n+1}. \] If \(a_7=120,\) then \(a_8\) is

solutions.text:
Let \(a_1=a\) and \(a_2=b.\) Repeated use of the recurrence gives \[ \begin{aligned} a_7&=5a+8b=120,\\ a_8&=8a+13b. \end{aligned} \] Modulo \(5,\) the first equation shows that \(b\) is a multiple of \(5.\) The positive possibilities are \(b=5,\) \(b=10,\) or \(b=15.\) The conditions \(b\gt a\gt0\) leave only \(b=10\) and \(a=8.\) Hence \(a_8=8(8)+13(10)=194.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Write \(a_7\) and \(a_8\) in terms of \(a_1\) and \(a_2\)
